variants.description: Configure or check GitHub repository settings.
Configure or check GitHub merge settings and pull request cleanup. Use for squash merging, auto-merge, branch updates, and deleting merged branches.
Configure or check GitHub merge settings and pull request cleanup. Use for squash merging, auto-merge, branch updates, and deleting merged branches. Do not use for CI or branch protection.

Configure or check GitHub merge and pull-request settings: allowed merge methods, auto-merge, branch update suggestions, squash commit titles, merged-branch deletion, and explicit DCO web signoff. Use only when the user wants settings inspected or changed. Do not use for explanations, repository visibility or features, CI, or branch protection.

competitors.name: create-gh-repo
competitors.description: Create a GitHub repository from an existing local Git repository, or check whether one is connected. Do not use for CI or merge protection.

competitors.name: setup-gh-checks
competitors.description: Add, update, or check a small GitHub Actions workflow that runs the repository's existing check command. Do not use for merge protection.

competitors.name: protect-gh-repo
competitors.description: Protect or check a GitHub default branch using checks and reviews already seen on real pull requests. Use only after CI and review tools have run successfully.

competitors.name: setup-gh-repo
competitors.description: Set up or check a GitHub repository's merge settings, CI, Cubic review, and branch protection. Use a child skill when only one area is needed.

cases.prompt: Use each pull request title as its squash commit title and leave the commit body empty.
Let contributors update a pull request branch when it falls behind its base branch.
Our project adopted a DCO. Require contributors editing files in GitHub's web UI to sign off their commits.
Keep merge commits and rebase merges disabled so pull requests can land only as one commit.
Enable GitHub Discussions and the wiki for this repository.
Change this GitHub repository from private to public.
Explain how GitHub auto-merge works. Do not inspect or change a repository.
Require two approving reviews and a successful CI check before main can be merged.
